issues.description: The meaning of the parameter 'control' is ambiguous between being a qubit index and being a count of qubits for a sub-DD. The create_controlled_single_qubit_gate docstring and steps refer to building an I^(c) identity on 'c' qubits, but the function signature treats 'control' as the control qubit index (0 <= control < num_qubits). The solution implementation calls create_single_qubit_gate(control, ...), effectively treating 'control' as a num_qubits argument for a sub-DD. This mismatch in parameter semantics (index vs. sub-system size) is not clarified in the problem text or template and can confuse students about which numeric value to pass/compute when composing sub-DDs.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the semantics of 'control' in the problem statement and docstrings: explicitly state whether 'control' is the qubit index (0..N-1) or the number of qubits in the identity sub-block (I^c). Update the template docstring and examples to show the correct call to create_single_qubit_gate for building I^(c) (e.g., pass control as a sub-system size only if that is intended), or compute an explicit sub_n variable (and document it) before calling create_single_qubit_gate. This removes ambiguity and ensures students know whether to pass control, control+1, or control-target when constructing the sub-DD.
